title: Largest XOR of Two Numbers in an Array

content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The maximum XOR obtainable from the array is 127.

content.problemStatement:
With an integer array `nums`, output *the largest result of* `nums[i] XOR nums[j]`, where `0 <= i <= j < n`.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: nums = [3,10,5,25,2,8]
Output: 28
Explanation: The maximum result is 5 XOR 25 = 28.
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: nums = [14,70,53,83,49,91,36,80,92,51,66,70]
Output: 127
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= nums.length <= 8 * 10^5`
* `0 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1`

notes: All values are non-negative and at most 2^31 - 1, so bits 30 through 0 are sufficient.
The returned maximum XOR also fits in the signed 32-bit non-negative range.
solution.approach: Use a greedy bit-by-bit construction of the answer. For each bit from 30 down to 0, tentatively set it and collect all array prefixes masked by the candidate. If two masked prefixes differ exactly by the candidate, that bit can be preserved; otherwise it cannot. This checks whether some pair of numbers realizes the candidate XOR prefix without enumerating all pairs.

better.complexity: Time O(31n), space O(31n) in the worst case.
better.description: Insert all values into a binary trie and, for each number, greedily follow the opposite bit when possible to maximize the XOR. The trie avoids pair enumeration and queries each number in one pass over the bit width.

optimal.description: Build the maximum XOR answer one bit at a time from most significant to least significant. For a tentative candidate, mask every number to the currently considered prefix. A bit is feasible exactly when some two prefixes differ by the candidate, because their lower bits cannot affect the already-fixed higher bits. This uses a reusable prefix set/table and avoids the large node count of a binary trie.

bruteForce.description: Check every pair (i,j), compute nums[i] XOR nums[j], and keep the maximum. This is the direct definition but requires quadratic pair enumeration.

solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space for the prefix set/table.

followUps: How would the solution change if the numbers could be signed 32-bit integers?
Can a binary trie be implemented with lower memory while keeping the same O(31n) time?
How would you adapt the approach if the input were streamed and could not all be stored at once?

learningObjectives: Recognize how bitwise greedy decisions can construct an optimum from most significant bit to least significant bit.
Use masked-prefix sets to test whether a target XOR prefix is realizable.
Compare the time and memory trade-offs of binary tries and hash-set prefix methods.
